title: Distilling and Adapting: A Topology-Aware Framework for Zero-Shot Interaction Prediction in Multiplex Biological Networks
claim: A multiplex network with several interaction layers can be encoded as one supra-adjacency matrix by combining per-layer and inter-layer adjacency matrices.
layout: 3 dashed rounded panels, left-to-right, with thick black arrows between them; the matrices sit in two dashed sub-boxes in the middle panel
description: The figure has three dotted rounded panels read left to right. The left panel shows a small example network with nodes a, b, c, d and e, with blue and orange edges for two relationship types. Next to it, the network is split into two stacked colored planes: Layer 1 in yellow and Layer 2 in orange. Dashed vertical lines connect the copies of the same node across layers. Thick arrows lead to the middle panel. The middle panel has two dashed boxes. One holds the intra-layer adjacency matrices A1 (red entries) and A2 (green entries). The other holds the inter-layer matrix C (blue entries). A final arrow leads to the right panel, which shows the combined supra-adjacency matrix Â = ⊕A_i + C. Its red, green and blue entries show where each block came from. The eye goes first to the colored matrices.
caption: Illustration of an example multiplex network and its supra-adjacency matrix. $A_1$ and $A_2$ are the layer-specific adjacency matrices for layer $1$ and $2$, $C$ is the inter-layer adjacency matrix, and $\hat{A}$ is the supra-adjacency matrix that represents the example multiplex network $\mathcal{G}$.
abstract: Multiplex Biological Networks (MBNs), which represent multiple interaction types between entities, are crucial for understanding complex biological systems. Yet, existing methods often inadequately model multiplexity, struggle to integrate structural and sequence information, and face difficulties in zero-shot prediction for unseen entities with no prior neighbourhood information. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for zero-shot interaction prediction in MBNs by leveraging context-aware representation learning and knowledge distillation. Our approach leverages domain-specific foundation models to generate enriched embeddings, introduces a topology-aware graph tokenizer to capture multiplexity and higher-order connectivity, and employs contrastive learning to align embeddings across modalities. A teacher-student distillation strategy further enables robust zero-shot generalization. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in interaction prediction for MBNs, providing a powerful tool for exploring various biological interactions and advancing personalized therapeutics.
